Lessons.Title: Compare Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 warm-up Estimation Exploration: Ladybug Length. The original picture shows a ladybug relative to a reference one-inch segment; pupils record a TOO LOW estimate, an ABOUT RIGHT estimate, and a TOO HIGH estimate. This is an intentionally approximate VISUAL task; no precise physical ladybug length may be certified from the photograph, nor should image pixels be treated as a calibrated ruler. The teacher checks the ordered estimates and explanations.

Activity1 Comparison Problems has four precise situations. SAME log: beetle crawls 2/8, caterpillar crawls 2/3 => caterpillar farther, because 2/8<2/3. A grasshopper 4cm and caterpillar 12/3cm => both 4cm, EQUAL. SAME branch: ladybug 3/8, ant 5/8 => ant farther, because3/8<5/8. SAME sidewalk: grasshopper jumps5/8, frog jumps5/6 => frog farther, because5/8<5/6. Students must state >, < or = AND provide argument.

Activity2 What Fraction Makes Sense? begins with exactly three ORIGINAL picture-hidden, juice-spilled expressions: 2/8 < n/8 (unknown numerator n>2); 3/6 = an unknown equivalent fraction (any proper or improper equivalent name equal to1/2 such as1/2,2/4,4/8); and 4/3 >4/d (unknown positive whole denominator d>3). The source asks 'as many numbers as you can'—do not impose one exact guessed missing digit. Do not invent additional obscured portions of a source image.

Activity2 then asks to name a fraction LESS than, GREATER than, and EQUIVALENT to each of the ORIGINAL bases 4/6 and3/4; the source materials also include a three-row note format listing 1/2. For 4/6 first-party examples are 3/6<4/6,5/6>4/6,2/3=4/6; for3/4 examples 2/4<3/4,4/4>3/4,6/8=3/4; for1/2 examples1/4<1/2,3/4>1/2,2/4=1/2. These are examples, not the only teacher-accepted responses.

Activity3 is clearly OPTIONAL in the 2021 source: Ultimate Locate and Label on an ORIGINAL number line from 0 to3. Preserve ALL ELEVEN exact fractions in this source order: 1/2,3/8,13/8,2/4,3/4,9/8,5/4,12/6,5/2,9/3,20/8. Equivalent positions include1/2=2/4, 5/2=20/8; also12/6=2 and9/3=3. Students draw and label exact positions with teacher evidence; a sole typed equality does not certify tick spacing.

Lesson synthesis consolidates same-numerator and same-denominator comparisons using >,<,= on a consistent same whole, represented with shapes or number lines. In the original on-device source, nine unique image URLs were inspected, including third-party ladybug/grasshopper photographs which are not copied into Edulytics. Publisher original Cool-down All Kinds of Comparisons is teacher-gated. Original standalone Student Task Statements PDF, tests, Stage D and academic approval remain unverified.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compare fractions of same whole
KeyConcepts.Definition: For positive fractions, use same unit whole and meaningful comparisons of equal-size parts.
KeyConcepts.Rule: With same denominator compare numerator; with same positive numerator compare denominator inversely.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent length measurements
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fractions of centimeters and whole-number lengths can be equal.
KeyConcepts.Example: Grasshopper and caterpillar have equal lengths in second original insect problem.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open missing numerator and denominator
KeyConcepts.Definition: Obscured expressions may have many mathematically valid completions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Source optional fraction positions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Improper fractions can be located on a zero-to-three number line.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Repeated fractions equivalent to same value belong at same location.

WorkedExamples.Title: Beetle versus caterpillar
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare2/8 and2/3 of the same log.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use same numerator, smaller denominator greater.
Steps: Two eighths is two small eighth-pieces.
Two thirds is two much larger thirds-pieces.

WorkedExamples.Title: Branch insect comparison
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare ladybug3/8 with ant5/8.
Steps: Three eighths compared to five eighths.

WorkedExamples.Title: Sidewalk jump comparison
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare grasshopper5/8 and frog5/6.
WorkedExamples.Method: Same numerator, sixths longer than eighths.
Steps: Five sixths span more than five eighths.

WorkedExamples.Title: Three obscured source comparisons
WorkedExamples.Question: Find sample completions for2/8<n/8,3/6=?,4/3>4/d.
WorkedExamples.Check: Do not claim one publisher answer.

WorkedExamples.Title: Optional 0–3 number line
WorkedExamples.Question: Locate 5/2 and20/8 on source line.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original optional list has eleven labels.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Give an exact measured ladybug length from image pixels.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source activity is explicitly visual estimation, not calibrated measurement.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Accept three ordered reasoned estimates with teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Force one exact answer for hidden juice labels.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original task deliberately asks many valid numbers.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Grade true mathematical constraints with appropriate denominator positivity.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Require optional eleven source fractions as mandatory.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source marks Ultimate Locate and Label OPTIONAL.

SummaryPoints: Warm-up ladybug length is an estimate, with too-low/about-right/too-high, not a calibrated numeric measurement.
Original insect outcomes: caterpillar farther; equal length; ant farther; frog farther.
Original juice-spilled prompts:2/8<n/8,3/6=unknown,4/3>4/d; many valid solutions.
Activity2 less/greater/equivalent to4/6 and3/4, plus source supporting format for1/2; examples not exhaustive.
OPTIONAL eleven fraction line 0–3 preserved exactly; repeated locations1/2=2/4 and5/2=20/8.
Publisher photos, PDF, gated Cool-down, tests and Stage D deferred.
